title: Star Blizzard refines phishing and malware delivery with the RedFlick technique
contentSnippet:
Since January 2026, Microsoft has observed Russian state threat actor Star Blizzard evolve their detection evasion capabilities through large-scale phishing campaigns, the use of accounts on compromised websites, and a novel malware delivery technique, tracked by Microsoft as “RedFlick”.

title: Using AI to chart a course for our post-quantum migration
contentSnippet: We’re building CryptoLabe, an internal AI-powered tool that discovers cryptography across our codebase, surfaces dependencies, and helps us progress toward a full post-quantum migration by 2029. Here’s what we’ve learned so far.

title: Building a certificate authority for the whole Internet
contentSnippet: Twelve years after launching Universal SSL, Cloudflare is applying to become a certificate authority. By combining an established root, an ACME-first approach, and Merkle Tree Certificates, we are building a post-quantum CA for the open web.

title: Adaptive application security for the AI era: how Cloudflare connects code, traffic, and intelligence to stop attacks
contentSnippet: Cloudflare introduces an adaptive security framework connecting risk discovery, agent governance, runtime protection, and AI-powered response in a continuous learning loop.

title: Building a post-quantum certificate authority with Merkle Tree Certificates
contentSnippet: As post-quantum signatures threaten to inflate TLS handshakes and certificate transparency logs, Merkle Tree Certificates offer a path to compact, auditable authentication. Cloudflare’s new certificate authority will support MTC issuance at scale.

title: We tested our own WAF with frontier AI models. Here’s what we found
contentSnippet: We built a WAF tester that adapted each request based on what the WAF blocked or passed. This helped us explore variations that a fixed test might miss. We ran it across six attack categories on an authorized staging environment and discovered detection gaps worth fixing.  Here’s how the loop worked, what got through, and what we did about it.

title: Introducing Threat Signals: agentic skills for open-source threat intelligence, free for every Cloudflare account
contentSnippet: We are expanding access to Cloudforce One's Threat Events Platform to every Cloudflare account and introducing Threat Signals. Threat Signals automatically parses open-source threat reporting, extracts structured indicators, and connects threat context directly to your WAF rules.

title: Is your domain using post-quantum encryption? Now you can see for yourself
contentSnippet: Cloudflare has added visibility into post-quantum (PQ) encryption in TLS 1.3 directly into HTTP Analytics, Log Explorer, and Logpush. Learn how to make sure your domain is protected with PQ encryption.

title: Enforce positive security with Cloudflare Application Profiles
contentSnippet: Cloudflare learns the structure of your HTTP requests and identifies deviations. You can add a positive security layer that helps reduce attack surface as AI makes it easier for attackers to generate and vary payloads.

title: Preventing quantum downgrade attacks against IPsec
contentSnippet: A sophisticated attacker with a quantum computer can exploit a protocol design flaw to downgrade post-quantum IPsec tunnels to classical crypto. We helped the IETF develop a transcript authentication extension to prevent these attacks.
